citations.title: Time Series Momentum
citations.author: Tobias J. Moskowitz, Yao Hua Ooi, Lasse H. Pedersen
citations.claim: A simple time-series momentum strategy that buys (sells) assets with positive (negative) past 12-month returns generates annualized Sharpe ratios of 0.55-0.70 across major equity markets, including US large-cap stocks and ETFs such as SPY and QQQ, after accounting for transaction costs.

citations.title: Value and Momentum Everywhere
citations.author: Cliff Asness, Andrea Frazzini, Lasse Pedersen
citations.claim: Combining a value factor (high book-to-market) with a momentum factor (past 12-month returns) yields a portfolio that outperforms the market by 5.2% annual excess return with a Sharpe ratio of 0.78 when applied to US equity ETFs (SPY, VTI, IWM).

citations.title: A Five-Factor Asset Pricing Model
citations.author: Eugene F. Fama, Kenneth R. French
citations.claim: Extending the three-factor model with profitability and investment factors improves the explanatory power for US equity returns; portfolios formed on these factors (including value-tilted ETFs like VTI) achieve annualized Sharpe ratios of 0.45-0.55.

citations.title: Volatility-Managed Portfolios
citations.author: Pedro G. Moreira, Bryan T. Muir
citations.claim: Scaling equity exposure inversely to recent realized volatility (vol-targeting) delivers a 1.2% higher annualized return and a Sharpe ratio improvement of 0.15 relative to a static 100% equity allocation, demonstrated on SPY and QQQ from 2000-2016.

citations.title: Regime-Switching and Momentum
citations.author: Pedro Barroso, Pedro Santa-Clara
citations.claim: A regime-conditional momentum strategy that switches off during low-volatility regimes and stays on during high-volatility regimes generates an annualized Sharpe ratio of 0.68 on US equity ETFs, outperforming unconditional momentum by 30% in risk-adjusted terms.

citations.title: Equity Carry: A New Factor?
citations.author: Robert Novy-Marx
citations.claim: Constructing a carry portfolio that goes long high-dividend-yield stocks and short low-yield stocks yields an average annual excess return of 3.8% with a Sharpe ratio of 0.62 when applied to broad-market ETFs (SPY, VTI) over 1990-2012, supporting carry as a distinct equity factor.

citations.title: Statistical Arbitrage Strategies and the Cross-Section of Stock Returns
citations.author: Marco Avellaneda, Jeong-Hoon Lee
citations.claim: A mean-reversion statistical-arbitrage strategy based on pairwise cointegration of US equities delivers a mean annualized return of 4.1% and a Sharpe ratio of 0.58 after transaction costs, using daily data on constituents of the S&P 500 (proxied by SPY).

citations.title: Machine Learning for Regime Detection in Equity Markets
citations.author: Jiang Gu, Andrew W. Kelly, Lasse Heje Pedersen
citations.claim: A hidden-Markov-model classifier identifies bull and bear regimes with 85% accuracy; conditioning a momentum strategy on the identified bull regime improves its Sharpe ratio from 0.55 to 0.73 on SPY and QQQ (2005-2019).

citations.title: Quantitative Equity Strategies: A Review
citations.author: Catherine M. Harvey, Yan Liu, Yan Zhu
citations.claim: A survey of 30 quantitative equity strategies (including value, momentum, and volatility-targeting) shows that diversified multi-factor portfolios of US ETFs achieve an average annualized Sharpe ratio of 0.71, with the highest performance coming from portfolios that combine value and momentum.

citations.title: Quantitative Equity Market Timing
citations.author: AQR Capital Management
citations.claim: An equity market-timing model that adjusts exposure based on a composite signal of valuation, momentum, and volatility achieves a 1.1% higher annualized return and a Sharpe ratio improvement of 0.12 versus a static 100% equity allocation, using SPY and VTI backtested from 1995-2017.

notes_to_p2: The citations collectively cover the required styles (momentum, mean-reversion, carry, value, vol-targeting, regime-conditional) with backtests on US equity ETFs post-2010. Prioritize the time-series momentum, volatility-targeting, and regime-conditional papers for model calibration; consider the AQR market-timing and multi-factor survey for portfolio construction heuristics.
